topics.topic: Decide whether a record-refused execution is a concluded attempt and state the cardinality-invariant exception
questions: Does an execution whose NodeExecution write was refused count as a concluded attempt, and if so how must the invariant express the new no-record exception?
Is a function execution whose NodeExecution write is refused a concluded attempt, and if so what exception must the formal invariant state?
Must the invariant exclude a function execution whose NodeExecution write the store refused, or is that execution not considered a concluded attempt?

judgement.why: P8 already decides that an execution whose record was not stored leaves no concluded record and that recovery executes the element again.

precedent.topic: Whether an execution with an unstored cleanup-failed record is concluded and how its record and attempt number are handled on replay
quotes:
If that record cannot be stored,
   the kernel process stops all the same, and recovery executes the element
   again, as it does every function element without a concluded record.

For one run, node and element, `attempt_number` is the ordinal of the
   element's NodeExecution M23 records: each NodeExecution written for the
   element takes the next number, from 1, whatever its status — an execution, a
   send, a pre-send failure, an owner's refusal, a skip, an upstream failure, the
   record of a mapped node over an empty list.
precedent.why: The failed write leaves no concluded record, so recovery repeats the element and the next successfully written NodeExecution takes the next ordinal; the unstored execution takes no attempt number.

topics.topic: Define attempt numbering and spool positions for recordless execution and recovery
questions: When a function execution leaves no NodeExecution because its record was refused, did that execution take an attempt number, and what attempt number and spool position must recovery use?

How can the first execution have a spool position containing an attempt number, and the recovery execution reuse that same number, when an execution that leaves no stored NodeExecution takes no number and files of two attempts are otherwise distinct SpooledFiles?

How can recovery retry “the same attempt number” when the carried State 2 obligation says an execution that leaves no stored NodeExecution takes no attempt number, and what attempt number keys any spool position created by the recordless execution?

judgement.why: P3 already decides that the caller provisionally uses the next NodeExecution ordinal for spooling and recovery reuses that position while no record exists.

precedent.topic: How recovery reuses an attempt-numbered spool position when an unrecorded execution takes no attempt number
quotes: record_change: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] attempt_number of a NodeExecution written by RecordRunProgressChange, RecordReadOutcomeChange, RecordOperationFailureChange or DecideApprovalChange, and of an EffectAttempt written by RecordAttemptInFlightChange, is one more than the number of NodeExecutions the element already has, the length of list_node_execution_rows_by_element for its ElementKey, and RequestApprovalChange gives the EffectApproval it writes that same next number as its attempt_number without writing a NodeExecution; RecordRunProgressChange writes its executions in (node_id, map_index) order with an absent map_index before index 0. A NodeExecution whose files were spooled before it is written carries the attempt_number its caller spooled them under, the element's next number read as the count of its NodeExecutions plus one; the change is refused with RefusedError, writing nothing, when that number is no longer the element's next, and no caller ever chooses another number.

spool_file: [BEHAVIOR] When no SpooledFile record names file's position, MUST publish content with publish_spool_entry for the data_directory open_store opened and file, which replaces a file no record names left at that position by a change that failed. The attempt_number of file is the element's next number as the caller read it; spool_file assigns none.
precedent.why: The later store contract makes the number provisional for spooling by having the caller read the element's next record ordinal, reuse it on recovery while no record exists, and commit that same number with the eventual NodeExecution.

topics.topic: Specify the required test for refused NodeExecution persistence, kernel stop, and one recovery re-execution
questions: What Required tests item must show the no-record exception, the kernel stop, and exactly one recovery re-execution?
Which Required tests item must show that the refused write leaves no NodeExecution, consumes no stored attempt number, stops the kernel, and causes exactly one recovery re-execution?

What Required test must show the newly introduced exception: that refusal of a function's NodeExecution write leaves no record, stops the kernel, and causes recovery to execute the function again while preserving the corrected cardinality invariant?

quotes:
Every concluded attempt at an element, every skipped node and every
   `upstream_failed` node writes exactly one NodeExecution M23 — an owner's
   resolution of an unknown outcome writes none (A11), and a function execution
   whose record the store refused writes none: the kernel stops and recovery
   executes it again (K-09, A03 rule 7).

A run with a three-element mapped node, a skipped node and an
   `upstream_failed` node holds exactly one NodeExecution per element, none of
   the mapped node's own, and one per skipped and per `upstream_failed` node; an
   owner's resolution of an unknown outcome adds none.
judgement.why: The Required tests omit the new record-refusal case, but the normative rule already fixes its behaviour, so no admissible product history gives two outcomes observable by an owner, agent, caller or external service.

topics.topic: Decide whether record-refusal handling applies only to NodeExecution or also to admission TrialExecution
questions: Does “a function execution” here mean only a run element whose record is a NodeExecution, or also a trial/admission execution whose record is a TrialExecution?

Does A15's store-refusal stop-and-reexecute rule apply only to a run's NodeExecution, or also to a function trial whose TrialExecution record is refused, which would add a second early-stop condition to A04?

judgement.why: P9 already distinguishes automatic recovery of recordless run elements from admission or explicit-try executions, which are repeated only by a later submission or try request.

precedent.topic: Whether and how startup recovery repeats unstored TrialExecutions from admission or explicit try, versus only run elements
quotes:
Admission executes the implementation on every case of the corpus, in corpus
   order, each as one TrialExecution M07, and never stops early — save for an
   execution whose cleanup cannot be confirmed: it is recorded `crashed` with
   `cleanup_failed` and the kernel stops (A03 rule 7), with no verdict
   recorded; after the restart a submission runs admission afresh.

Trying an implementation (State 0 action), by any agent,
   executes an existing implementation on the cases of its contract version's
   corpus that the request names, all of them when it names none, in corpus
   order, records one TrialExecution per case and returns them.

On start, before the surface accepts a request, the kernel turns every
   `in_flight` EffectAttempt into `unknown` (A11 rule 4) and then derives every
   run that has not ended — `running`, `awaiting_approval` or `pending` — again
   from its records, oldest first in store order, rewriting a stored status or
   waiting point that lags them (a decided approval, a resolved attempt, an
   outcome whose run change was lost), and advances, as the
   kernel actor, every run that derivation leaves `running`: a
   function element without a
   concluded record is executed again, which is safe because it has no effect; a `read`
   element without one is sent again; an operation element of another class with
   neither a concluded record nor an EffectAttempt was never sent and is advanced
   as if reached for the first time — an approved, unused approval covers it
   only while the rebuilt request has its `request_digest` (A10 rules 1 and 7).
precedent.why: Automatic startup replay is defined for function elements of unfinished runs; admission resumes only through a later submission, and an explicit try is repeated only by another try request.

topics.topic: Define which store-refusal outcomes and transaction boundary trigger kernel stop and recovery re-execution
questions: Exactly which store outcomes count as the store refusing the record and trigger a kernel stop and re-execution?
Exactly which store outcomes count as the record being refused, and at what transaction boundary does this rule apply?

judgement.why: P4 already decides the atomic transaction boundary and the store outcomes that write nothing when a NodeExecution cannot be recorded.

precedent.topic: Store outcomes that count as refusing a NodeExecution record
quotes: record_change: [BEHAVIOR] MUST apply the one StoreChange given in one SQLite transaction that either writes every record the variant lists or nothing; it writes no record the variant does not list and trusts the caller for every decision of the caller's rule, checking only its own invariants: attempt numbers, unique and existing identities, existing linked records, and no edit of an immutable record. It checks no status of the record a lifecycle change updates and sets that change's fields whatever status the record has: the status a change may start from is the caller's rule, and one request ends before the next begins (A18), so no other request can have changed it meanwhile. A record of a kind the security-boundary note names never updated is only ever written once; a lifecycle change updates the fields its variant sets on the one record the change names, in place, and no other field of a written record ever changes.

record_change: [VALIDATION_ERROR] For RecordAttemptOutcomeChange and RecoverInFlightChange MUST raise RefusedError, writing nothing, when the named attempt's attempt_number is no longer one more than the number of NodeExecutions of its element; the concluding NodeExecution then takes that attempt's number. Any other broken invariant — a linked record missing, or an identity already present for a record that is written once — or a failed transaction raises StoreInternalError with nothing written.
precedent.why: The later store contract defines record changes as local atomic SQLite transactions and states that every refusal or failed transaction writes nothing, so an unknown committed-but-unacknowledged outcome is not an allowed store result.

topics.topic: Decide whether the A15 consequence applies only to durable concluded work
questions: Must the consequence be narrowed to durable concluded work, since the kernel can execute a function without leaving any trace record?

quotes:
The trace is the only source the kernel uses to explain or continue a run;
   process logs are never an input to a kernel decision.

Every concluded attempt at an element, every skipped node and every
   `upstream_failed` node writes exactly one NodeExecution M23 — an owner's
   resolution of an unknown outcome writes none (A11), and a function execution
   whose record the store refused writes none: the kernel stops and recovery
   executes it again (K-09, A03 rule 7).
judgement.why: The texts define the trace as the kernel's decision source and expressly define the unstored physical execution as leaving no concluded record, so the consequence does not promise a record of every sandbox invocation.
